_comment: Claude model selection policy (Issue #100). EXPLICIT WINS: a task that names a model gets exactly that model or is refused — never a substitute. ABSENT MEANS CHOSEN, NEVER INHERITED: when a task names no model the executor picks haiku/sonnet/opus from the deterministic signal table below and always passes --model, so the Claude CLI's own ambient default (today: the fable family) is never what runs. Fable is auto_selectable:false everywhere: it runs only when a task asks for it by name. `model` values are the ONLY strings that ever reach the --model argv position; an inbound task can never pass a string through, it can only select a key that already exists here.

fable-5.1.disabled_reason: not offered by the installed Claude CLI (2.1.251 ships fable only as claude-fable-5); set enabled:true here — no code change — once `claude --model claude-fable-5-1` is accepted on this host

auto._comment: Signals are additive integers. Every contributing signal is recorded on the task and in the model_selected event, so a choice is always explainable. Terms are plain lowercase substrings (never regexes) and are deliberately chosen NOT to occur in the GitHub bridge's own instruction boilerplate — tests/model-selection-policy-test.js pins that.
